title: Keyboard and gamepad input mapped to game actions
when: The game must read the keyboard and game controllers through one layer of named actions like jump or fire, polled once per simulation tick.
prompt:
Goal: Game code asks input.isDown("jump") and never looks at raw keys or button indexes.
Steps:
1. js/input.js holds bindings = { left: ["ArrowLeft", "KeyA"], right: ["ArrowRight", "KeyD"], jump: ["Space", "KeyW"], fire: ["KeyJ"] } using event.code, so AZERTY layouts keep the same physical keys.
2. keydown and keyup update a Set of held codes; preventDefault only for bound codes so browser shortcuts survive.
3. Clear the Set on window blur so keys do not stick after switching apps.
4. Each tick read navigator.getGamepads(); for pads with mapping === "standard" use buttons[0] for jump, buttons[2] for fire and axes[0] for horizontal with a dead zone of 0.2.
5. Listen to gamepadconnected and gamepaddisconnected to show a short "Controller connected" status line.
6. input.poll() at the start of update computes pressed (down now, up last tick) and released per action.
7. input.axis("moveX") returns -1 to 1, merging keys and stick and keeping the larger magnitude.
Quality bar:
- Holding a key never auto repeats a jump.
- Unplugging a pad mid game stops its input without errors.
Pitfalls:
- event.key, which changes with shift and keyboard layout.
- Caching the Gamepad object; some browsers hand out a fresh snapshot on every call.
- Reading pressed edges inside render, so quick taps between ticks get lost.
Verify:
- [ ] pressed fires once per physical press.
- [ ] Switching apps while holding right does not keep moving.
- [ ] Stick drift under 0.2 is ignored.
Output: js/input.js exporting bindings, poll, isDown, pressed and axis.

examples.input: suporte a controle de videogame no meu jogo de navegador
examples.output: action map over event.code plus standard gamepad polling with dead zone and press edges
